items.title: $100 to a Debian Developer who can get the Fresh IDE into Trixie (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I use Debian 13 in a regulated industry and I'm teaching people how to code in the context of large projects and TUI. I want to use Fresh (https://getfresh.dev/). This is because Fresh is easier to learn quickly than vim & emacs, and more like an IDE than micro & nano, and more favorable for compliance auditing because of its core-and-plugins architecture and code using Rust. I would like to donate toward this goal. I can afford to offer $100 to any Debian Developer who has the suitable skill and trust to accomplish this. Success looks like this: create a new Debian 13 server, type "apt install fresh-editor" (or whatever name), and it works. No third-party apt sources needed, because I have compliance reasons. Here's the GitHub issue: https://github.com/sinelaw/fresh/issues/2169 I'm not affiliated with Fresh in any way, other than as a early adopter user. If you look at the GitHub issues, I'm also offering $100 each for helping with Fresh display issues on MacBooks, and for adding Fresh ePub capabilities. I'm doing this because I believe in funding open source as much as possible. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48347180 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: Ouijit, an open-source task and terminal manager for coding agents (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hi HN, I'm working on Ouijit. It's a project and task-based terminal session manager that provides a few basic but useful tools for agent workflows: - Terminal sessions in Ouijit have access to the ouijit CLI, and supported agents (Claude, Codex, Pi) can work with it out of the box to manage tasks and customize a personal development workflow - Tasks live on a kanban board that supports hooks for task lifecycle events (eg. 'Run this script when a task moves to 'in progress') I've found this simple combination to be very expressive and flexible for adapting to changing workflows. I made the V1 a couple months ago for fun, and have kept at it since a friend shared they had logged an 8 hour work session in it. Along the way I've baked in lots of what I believe are table-stakes for this type of tool, like task isolation via Git worktrees, agent working/idle status with sound and notifications, diff/markdown plan/URL previews, and support for VM sandboxing using Lima. It's free and open source with no login or telemetry, so feedback is highly appreciated. Github: https://github.com/ouijit/ouijit Website: https://ouijit.com Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48347043 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
